[00:01:31] Priya Kapoor: Important detail: streaming can add overhead depending on prefix caching and token flush frequency, so we usually recommend an initial benchmark measuring tokens/sec and end-to-end p95 with streaming enabled.
[00:01:42] Lina Gomez: From security side we need SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integration for encryption of model inputs — we can't have PHI leave our VPC until evaluation is done. How does Redwood handle that?
[00:01:53] Alex Chen: We have three deployment modes. Hosted for fastest onboarding and predictable perf for many customers; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with network isolation and SLA; Private is VPC or on-prem where we can run the control plane in your environment and integrate with your KMS. For PHI we'd usually recommend Dedicated with private networking or Private deployment depending on compliance needs.
[00:02:12] Dana Ruiz: So for the initial pilot, we might do dedicated to get the perf SLA without exposing data?
[00:02:17] Priya Kapoor: That makes sense. Dedicated lets you pin instance types and capacity. For benchmarking, we'd run a token/sec sustained test plus concurrency ramp to estimate autoscale and p95 under load.
[00:02:28] Ethan Park: question: how do you measure p95 for streaming? is it time-to-first-token or time-to-last-token?

[00:03:11] Alex Chen: Also routing plays a role — for Dedicated we can reserve nodes and guarantee capacity. Hosted is multi-tenant so p95 is usually well-characterized but peak isolation can be less strict unless you buy reserved capacity or Dedicated.

[00:03:44] Ethan Park: So if we have 50 streams doing 150 tokens each, that's 7.5k tokens per burst, but sustained depends on frequency. we need to model concurrency and bursts.
[00:03:54] Priya Kapoor: Exactly. We'll help you model steady-state tokens/sec and peak bursts. Our benchmark template will let you plug in your distribution.
[00:04:02] Jared Cole: What about fallback? if capacity's tight do you degrade quality, switch to smaller model, or queue requests?
[00:04:09] Alex Chen: We support graceful fallbacks: model variants (smaller/quantized), region routing, and configurable timeouts/queueing. For clinician UX we usually prefer smaller model fallback or cached templates for predictable latency instead of queuing.

[00:05:56] Priya Kapoor: quick note on streaming benchmarks — measure per-token serialization overhead and network flush intervals. For web clients, small chunk frequencies can increase TTFT; we typically recommend 64-128 token flush windows for balance.
[00:06:09] Dana Ruiz: Interesting. We also use a lots of retrieval augmentation with embeddings. Any impact on latency?
[00:06:14] Priya Kapoor: RAG adds retrieval latency; common pattern is to prefetch or cache embeddings and do retrieval async. We can architect the flow so the model call sees prepared context, minimizing added p95.

[00:06:28] Alex Chen: Private can run on customer GPUs; we ship a control plane and runtime that can use your GPU fleet. We'll provide sizing templates based on your target tokens/sec and concurrency.
